title: test(types): the JoinedReportBlock pin compiles on the installed spec and on spec main, and trips at the bump (objectui#10916)
body:
Fixes #10916
Clause-②: no — a test-side tripwire and the ledger text beside it move to what spec `main` now says; no published type, no export and no accepted document changes (the local `JoinedReportBlock` interface and the `index.ts` exports are untouched).

⚠️ Generic parameters are written as UPPERCASE WORDS in this body (for example "IsUnknown OF SpecJoinedReportBlock"), never in angle brackets: GitHub's body sanitizer deletes tag-shaped fragments on save, and backticks do not protect them (AGENTS.md, "GitHub mutates body BYTES"). Diagnostics are quoted by code and text, without the file's line and column, per AGENTS.md #11.

## What was red, and why the pin was right to go red

objectstack#20369 (`681868ca7`) removed the bare `z.ZodTypeAny` annotation from `JoinedReportBlockSchema` on objectstack `main`. The inverted pin `_specJoinedReportBlockIsStillUntyped` (`true satisfies` IsUnknown OF SpecJoinedReportBlock) in `packages/types/src/__tests__/report-chart-query-spec-parity.test.ts` then failed with TS1360 ("Type 'true' does not satisfy the expected type 'false'.") on the Spec Main Shape Gate, which compiles every head against spec built from objectstack `main`. Its docblock said that failure is the instruction: re-run the triage and burn it down.

The pull-request type-check compiles the SAME file against the INSTALLED spec, the published 17.4.0 (the newest release on npm, published 2026-09-09, so before #20369). There the type is still `unknown`. Whatever stands in the file has to compile against both until a spec bump installs a release carrying #20369.

## The re-run triage: spec `main` against the local interface, member by member

Read with the TypeScript checker off the source-built spec's `dist` (objectstack `df3ba164a588`); `JoinedReportBlock` is neither `any` nor `unknown` there and has no index signature.

| member | local `JoinedReportBlock` (`spec-report.ts`) | spec `main` `JoinedReportBlock` (input) | verdict |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `name` | `string`, required | `string`, required (snake_case at runtime) | agree |
| `type` | optional `tabular` / `summary` / `matrix` | the same enum, optional (defaults to `tabular`) | agree |
| `label`, `description` | string, or an object with `default` and `translations` | string, or an inline locale map whose every value is a string | diverge: the local object arm is not a spec label |
| `columns` | REQUIRED array of column OBJECTS (`field`, `aggregate`, ...) | optional array of dimension NAMES (matrix across-axis) | one name, two concepts |
| `objectName` | declared | not declared; the closed schema refuses it (its alias table points at `dataset`) | local-only |
| `groupingsDown`, `groupingsAcross` | declared | not declared; refused | local-only |
| `filter` | declared | not declared; refused (alias table points at `runtimeFilter`) | local-only |
| `chart` | declared | retired by objectstack#20161, refused with the retirement prescription | local-only |
| index signature | `[k: string]: unknown` | none (closed schema) | diverge |
| `dataset`, `rows`, `values`, `runtimeFilter`, `order` | not declared | declared (the ADR-0021 dataset-bound selection) | spec-only |

**Verdict.** The spec type is now precise, and it describes a DIFFERENT shape: guard case 2c on spec `main`, no longer 2b. The local interface is the legacy inline-query block, and the spec's closed schema refuses every one of its five local-only keys. So it is derivable, but not by a re-export beside the local interface: the burn-down REPLACES the published `JoinedReportBlock` (and the `blocks` of `JoinedSpecReport`) with the spec's type. That changes a published type, so it is its own slice, and it cannot land before the bump, because against the installed spec the derived type would be `unknown`. Nothing in this tree reads the local interface's legacy members (from a grep of the five local-only keys and a reading of the renderer, not a runtime probe): the joined branch of `DatasetReportRenderer` reads dataset-bound blocks, and the local type is only re-exported and used by `JoinedSpecReport`.

## The chosen shape, and the precedent it follows

objectui#10080 (PR #10089) is the precedent for "the gate compiles against spec `main`, the PR check against the installed pin": it kept both jobs of the red declaration and changed its form so the file compiles against both specs, then proved both legs with a control. objectui#3177 (case 2c for `NavigationItem`) is the precedent for what replaces an `IsAny` / IsUnknown pin once the spec is typed: per-key probes that each stop compiling the day that one divergence moves. This PR does both. The guard now has two halves, because two different runs read two different specs:

- **Compile time, both runs.** A state pin, `_specJoinedReportBlockTyping`, admits `erased` and `typed` and refuses `any`; the `IsAny` pin stays as it was. On a typed spec, seven divergence and agreement probes (`_localBlockIsNotTheSpecBlock`, `_specOnlyBlockKeys`, `_localOnlyBlockKeys`, `_blockColumnsAreTwoConcepts`, `_blockLabelObjectArmIsNotASpecLabel`, `_blockNameAgrees`, `_blockTypeAgrees`) record the triage above and stop compiling the day one of them moves, on the Spec Main Shape Gate first. On the erased spec they are not asked (`OnTypedSpec`), since an erased type declares no member to compare.
- **Test time, the installed spec only.** The Spec Main Shape Gate type-checks and runs no test, so a vitest tripwire can act on the INSTALLED spec alone. It reads the installed spec's built declarations with the TypeScript checker, and it fails on the first bump past the published 17.4.0. If that release types the block, the failure is the burn-down's start signal: derive the published interface in its own slice, and delete the state pin's `erased` arm so that an erasure stops compiling again. If that release still erases the block, the spec erased it again, which is an upstream regression; the `erased` arm loses its licence either way. A lit control (`ReportSort` must read `typed`) keeps the reader from passing vacuously.

⚠️ **Declared limit.** An erasure on objectstack `main` BEFORE that bump cannot be told apart, at the type level, from the installed 17.4.0: both are the same bare `z.ZodTypeAny`. The state pin therefore admits it on the gate. The producer's own pin covers that window (`packages/spec/src/ui/joined-report-block-type.test.ts` in objectstack, landed with #20369), and the tripwire's version row catches it at the bump at the latest.

Nothing was skipped, disabled or ts-ignored, and no workflow changed. The ledger row (the `JoinedReportBlock` ALLOW entry in `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs`, which is objectui#3162's ledger in machine-readable form) and that script's case-2b header now say what is true of both specs, and when the burn-down fires.

## Both compile legs, from committed state

Legs taken with `pnpm run type-check` in `packages/types` (all three `tsc` programs, `tsconfig.test.json` included). The spec-`main` legs follow the gate's own procedure: `@objectstack/spec` built from objectstack `df3ba164a588` (a detached worktree, `pnpm install --frozen-lockfile --filter @objectstack/spec...`, `pnpm --filter @objectstack/spec build`), `npm pack --ignore-scripts`, then `node scripts/spec-main-shape-gate.mjs inject` into this worktree's install. The inject printed its consumer list and re-pointed `zod` to 4.6.1, as the gate does. The installed legs ran after a clean reinstall, with the gate's injection marker confirmed absent.

| leg | spec under the compiler | tree | result |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| installed, before | published 17.4.0, block is `unknown` | `733fd5ac6` (base) | exit 0, 0 diagnostics |
| spec `main`, before | source-built `df3ba164a588`, block typed | `733fd5ac6` | **exit 2, 1 diagnostic**: TS1360 "Type 'true' does not satisfy the expected type 'false'." at `_specJoinedReportBlockIsStillUntyped` (the same diagnostic the gate reports) |
| spec `main`, after | same injected build | `8ce61bad3` | **exit 0, 0 diagnostics** |
| installed, after | published 17.4.0 restored | `8ce61bad3`, and again at head `22226a8e9` | **exit 0, 0 diagnostics** |

The two commits after `8ce61bad3` touch only `scripts/` and `.changeset/`, which no `packages/types` program reads.

⚠️ Narrowed on purpose: the gate runs `turbo run type-check` over every package. Locally only `@object-ui/types` was compiled against spec `main`, because it is the only package the gate reported and the only one this diff touches. The full farm is the gate's own run on this head.

## The tripwire, fired for real

Under the injected spec-`main` install, `pnpm exec vitest run packages/types/src/__tests__/report-chart-query-spec-parity.test.ts` gives **1 failed, 46 passed (47)**. The one failure is the typing row, with its message: "the installed @objectstack/spec 17.4.0 now types JoinedReportBlock — this is the bump the burn-down is owed at. [...] expected 'typed' to be 'erased'". The lit control and the version row pass (a source-built `main` still reports version 17.4.0). Under the installed spec the same file gives **47 passed (47)**.

## Ablations, each proved on disk

All through `ablation-replace.mjs` (objectstack `scripts/`) in wrap mode. For every leg the tool reported "mutation landed", and after it "restored: blob == HEAD (`a1b2c707461e`) and `git diff HEAD` is empty".

Spec `main` injected, `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`:

| leg | mutation | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A1 | drop `order` from `_specOnlyBlockKeys`' expected set | TS1360 at that pin |
| A2 | drop `chart` from `_localOnlyBlockKeys`' expected set | TS1360 at that pin |
| A3 | spec `columns` expected as `number[]` | TS1360 at `_blockColumnsAreTwoConcepts` |
| A4 | state pin without its `typed` arm | TS1360 "Type '"typed"' does not satisfy the expected type '"erased"'." |
| A5 | state pin without its `erased` arm | 0 diagnostics (the burn-down's future edit is valid on a typed spec) |
| A6 | `_blockTypeAgrees` compares `name` against `type` | TS1360 at that pin |
| A7 | local label replaced by a plain string in `_blockLabelObjectArmIsNotASpecLabel` | TS1360 at that pin |

Installed 17.4.0:

| leg | mutation | result |
| --- | --- | --- |
| A5 | state pin without its `erased` arm | TS1360 "Type '"erased"' does not satisfy the expected type '"typed"'." (the arm is load-bearing today) |
| A1 | as above | 0 diagnostics: the typed-spec probes are not asked of an erased spec, as declared |
| V | tripwire version row expects `17.3.0` | vitest: that row alone red, 1 failed, 46 passed |

⚠️ The first attempt at A1, A2 and A5 on spec `main` was a no-op. The replacement text was a substring of the anchor, so `ablation-replace` refused it ("the replacement count moved 1 to 1", paraphrased) and restored. Those three legs were re-run in `--delete` mode, and the table shows the re-run.

## Tests and gates, on head `22226a8e9`

- `pnpm exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 packages/types/`: **264 files, 5856 tests, all passed** (installed spec).
- Every test that references `scripts/check-spec-symbol-derivation.mjs` (31 files, `scripts/__tests__` and package suites): **31 files, 630 tests, all passed**.
- `pnpm check:spec-symbols`: exit 0 ("0 untriaged collisions in 0 packages").
- `check-changeset-presence`: RED first ("1 source file(s) of 1 released package(s) changed, and this change adds no changeset"). That gate counts every file under a released package's `src/`, tests included. So this PR carries `.changeset/10916-joined-report-block-pin-two-specs.md` with an EMPTY frontmatter, and the gate then reads exit 0 ("declared as releasing nothing").
- Exit 0 as well: `check-changeset-no-major`, `check-changeset-fixed`, `check-changeset-overwrite`, `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals`, `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new citations), `check:test-path-roots`, `check:installed-pin-claims`, `check:shell-escape-residue`, `check:vi-mock-specifiers`, `check:vi-mock-inherit`.
- `check-governed-queue-guard --test` on the three paths: NOT GOVERNED.
- eslint (`--no-inline-config`) on the two changed source files: 2 files linted, 0 errors, 0 warnings. Narrowed on purpose; the config enables no type-aware linting, so this diff cannot move the verdict on an untouched file.
- NOT MEASURED, prerequisite: `check:spec-floors` needs every package built (it reports `no-artifact` for all 19 spec consumers in an unbuilt worktree); this diff moves no manifest or `dist`.

## The second slice this owes (not in this PR)

At the first spec bump past 17.4.0, derive `JoinedReportBlock` from `@objectstack/spec/ui` and converge `JoinedSpecReport`'s `blocks`. Reading: **Clause-② yes (narrowing)**. The published local type accepts any key through its index signature and types the legacy members; the spec's is closed and dataset-bound. It should land WITH the bump: on a typed spec, `JoinedSpecReport` intersects the spec's `blocks` (from `ReportParsed`) with the local ones, which makes `columns` both names and objects (read from the two declarations, not compiled).

## Acceptance notes

- objectui#3162 is CLOSED and its body still records the 17.2.0 verdict for this symbol. It is not edited here; the in-tree ledger row is.
- `spec-derived-unions.test.ts` keeps its batch-8 note that this symbol was "STILL erased"; that note is a dated reading at spec 17.2.0 and is left as history.

This change was made in Claude Code session `https://claude.ai/code/session_01DuWo5bdP9SdVebamn99GGk`.
